standard.title: Moving Body and Manipulating Objects
standard.description: experiment with different ways of moving their body safely and manipulating objects and space
standard.prior_knowledge: No prior HPE curriculum. Students bring informal movement experience and basic spatial awareness from daily life. No prior structured experimentation with movement choices.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students experiment with different ways of moving their body safely and manipulating objects and space, making judgements about effectiveness and demonstrating spatial awareness.

nodes.label: Suggest and test movement choices
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can suggest different ways to move or use equipment and test them, making simple judgements about which are most effective.
nodes.minimum_width: Suggest at least one alternative way to move or use equipment in a play context and test it.
nodes.typical_width: Suggest and test multiple movement approaches across different play situations; make and share simple judgements about which approaches work best and which they prefer.
wider: Suggest and test movement choices in outdoor and natural settings, adapting to different terrain
Experiment with non-standard equipment or everyday objects in movement tasks
Compare movement strategies with peers, discussing differences in effectiveness
nodes.hinge_reason: The capacity to deliberately experiment with movement — rather than simply move habitually — is the cognitive foundation of this standard. Students who only replicate demonstrated movements cannot access the investigative intent of this descriptor or the Y1-2 equivalent which demands conclusions about effectiveness.

response_modes.reason: Scaffold the experiment cycle explicitly: 'Try this way. Try another way. Which worked better? Why?' Simple verbal or gestural reflection is sufficient at Foundation — the thinking process is what matters.
Varied play equipment and environments give students more raw material for genuine experimentation rather than replicating teacher demonstrations.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Experimenting across varied contexts — natural environments, non-standard equipment, peer comparison — develops genuine movement problem-solving disposition, not just compliance with movement patterns.
success_criteria: Attempts at least two different approaches to a movement task or equipment use
Makes a simple statement about which approach worked better or which they preferred

nodes.label: Persistence and resilience in movement
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can persist with movement challenges, demonstrating resilience when a movement or task is difficult.
nodes.minimum_width: Attempt a challenging movement task at least twice, persisting through difficulty.
nodes.typical_width: Demonstrate persistence across a range of movement challenges; describe or show what they do when a movement is hard (try again, modify approach).
wider: Reflect on how persistence felt — linking emotional experience to physical challenge
Observe and discuss a peer's persistence, connecting to fair play and encouragement
Engage with movement challenges in outdoor settings where uncertainty and variability are higher

response_modes.reason: Persistence is cultivated through repeated low-stakes challenge, not through a single difficult task. Design movement circuits with graduated difficulty and celebrate effort explicitly.

success_criteria: Attempts a challenging movement task more than once without giving up
Shows or describes a self-regulation strategy when movement is difficult (e.g. trying again, pausing)

nodes.label: Safety in shared movement spaces
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can demonstrate spatial awareness when moving around and through environments, and participate in games with awareness of personal safety.
nodes.minimum_width: Move through a shared play space with awareness of others, avoiding collisions; follow basic game safety rules.
nodes.typical_width: Demonstrate spatial awareness in indoor and outdoor environments; participate in games that require awareness of boundaries, rules and safe use of equipment; describe a safety rule in a game context.
wider: Navigate outdoor and natural environments with varying spatial demands (open fields, obstacle courses, natural features)
Identify and explain safety considerations for a specific equipment type used in games
Design a simple safety rule for a class game and explain its purpose

response_modes.reason: Safety awareness is context-dependent — students who understand indoor gym safety may not transfer it automatically to outdoor or water environments. Vary settings to build genuine awareness.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Outdoor and equipment-specific safety contexts offer meaningful application of spatial awareness beyond the classroom setting.
success_criteria: Moves through a shared space without colliding with others or equipment
Follows a safety rule in a game context and can name it when asked
